Role Name: HR Business Partner

Department: People

Location: San Carlos




ABOUT 1X

We're building humanoid robots that work in home - doing the chores, handling the tasks, and giving people their time back. Simple, but it's not.



To do this right, we have to solve robotics, AI, manufacturing - at the same time, at scale, in a form factor that has to be safe enough to live with your family. If you're inspired by this, you'll thrive here. We've been at this since 2014 and we're at the point where the hard problems are behind us and the hard work is in front of us.



NEO is our flagship - a home robot designed to move, learn, and operate in the real world alongside real people. We're not demoing it - we're shipping it. We're excited to meet you, if this excites you.



If you've spent your career working on problems that matter and want to see them actually reach the world - this is that moment. We're scaling, we're hiring with intention, and we need people who want to build something that will genuinely change how humans spend their time - safely creating abundance for all.




ABOUT THE TEAM

The People team builds the organization that builds NEO. We work alongside leaders across 1X so teams can hire well, grow their people, and keep moving fast as the company scales. This role is embedded in our software engineering org, where the pace is high and the work is getting the robot to ship.




YOUR CHARTER

The mission of this role is to be the embedded HR partner to 1X's software engineering org, so its managers get the coaching and support they need and its senior leader can stay focused on building.



You report to our Director of HR, who stays the main HR contact for the org's senior leader. You own the partnership with everyone at scale. You sit in on team meetings, meet regularly with managers and directors, coach them through hard conversations, and bring what you hear back to HR leadership as clear themes and recommendations. The org is about 100 people today and growing. When the business needs it, you flex to support other groups.




KEY OUTCOMES

 - Own a weekly or biweekly rhythm with the org's managers and directors, so people issues come up early and reach HR leadership with a recommendation attached.

 - Coach engineering managers through performance conversations, feedback, and difficult situations, so these are handled well by the managers themselves and don't escalate to the org's senior leader.

 - Lead employee relations matters and investigations for the org, with outcomes that are fair, well documented, and compliant with California employment law.

 - Partner with Talent Acquisition as the org's hiring liaison, so headcount plans, hiring priorities, and onboarding for new managers keep pace as the team grows.

 - Deliver performance, promotion, and compensation cycles for the org on time, with managers prepared for calibration and the conversations that follow.




KEY COMPETENCIES

 - Engineering fluency: understands how software teams and engineering managers work, and earns their credibility quickly.

 - Manager coaching: helps managers own hard conversations instead of taking those conversations over.

 - Org listening: builds trust across a team, hears things early, and turns them into clear themes and next steps.

 - Startup execution: gets things done with little process and no big HR support structure, and is comfortable shifting to where the work is.

 - Sound judgment and discretion on sensitive employee matters.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of HR experience, including 3+ years as an embedded HR Business Partner to a defined client group.

 - Experience partnering with engineering, software, or other technical teams at a technology company.

 - Demonstrated ability to coach managers through performance management and to lead employee relations investigations, with working knowledge of California employment law.

 - Ability to work onsite in San Carlos, CA.




PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Experience at a startup or high-growth technology company, especially in robotics, hardware, or AI.

 - Experience supporting a team through a period of fast hiring alongside a recruiting team.

 - Familiarity with using engagement, attrition, and performance data to spot trends and inform leaders.

 - PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP certification.




WHAT DOES A SUCCESSFUL 1X TEAM MEMBER LOOK LIKE

Team members at 1X who thrive here are builders. They move fast, own their work completely, and treat time like it's the one thing you can't get back - because it is. They say what they mean, finish what they start, and hold themselves to a standard before anyone has to ask. We push each other to be better, and we do it with honesty and respect.

$130,000 - $180,000/ + Equity




BENEFITS

 - Generous paid time off, company holidays, and parental leave

 - 401(k) plan with company match (100% on the first 3% of contributions, 50% on the next 2%)

 - Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Health Savings Accounts (HSA) options

 - Commuter benefits (transit and parking)

 - Short-term and long-term disability, and life insurance

Position Overview

Axelera AI is a fast-growing AI semiconductor company headquartered in Eindhoven, building high-performance, energy-efficient AI acceleration hardware and software, from the Metis AI platform for edge inference to next-generation AI processing units. We are scaling quickly: new customers, new partners, new markets, and a growing volume of complex commercial deals across the global semiconductor supply chain.

We are looking for an experienced commercial lawyer to be the engine of our commercial legal function. You will close deals, build the playbooks and processes that let the business move fast without taking on unmanaged risk, and lead how legal operates day to day, with AI in the loop so a lean team delivers more with less. This is a hands-on role with real scope to shape the function as it grows.



Key responsibilities:

Commercial contracting

 - Draft, review and negotiate a high volume of commercial agreements: customer, distribution, reseller and OEM/ODM agreements; sales terms and EULAs; supply and manufacturing agreements (foundry, OSAT, component suppliers); technology and IP licences; software and SaaS agreements; evaluation, early access and development agreements; R&D collaboration and consortium agreements; services and vendor agreements; and MOUs, LOIs and partnership terms.

 - Act as the trusted, pragmatic adviser to Sales, Product, Engineering, Operations and Finance, giving clear, commercial risk calls at pace.

 - Advise on key semiconductor and AI issues: IP ownership and licensing, warranties and liability caps, product liability, export controls and sanctions, data protection and the EU AI Act.

 - Support the CFO and Head of Legal on strategic matters, including corporate transactions and board-level work, as needed.

Playbooks and scale

 - Build AI-ready contract playbooks, fallback positions and approval matrices so AI tools and the business can handle routine deals with minimal Legal involvement.

 - Create and own a library of standard templates for our core agreement types (e.g. NDA, customer terms, evaluation, distributor, supplier) aligned to our risk appetite.

 - Train commercial teams on contract basics, negotiation positions and when to escalate to Legal.

Legal operations

 - Lead legal operations: intake and triage, prioritisation, SLAs and reporting on legal workload and turnaround.

 - Own the legal tech and AI stack: select, implement and continuously improve AI review and drafting tools, CLM, e-signature and the contract repository, automating repeatable work end to end.

 - Own contract lifecycle management, including obligation tracking, renewals and keeping contract records complete and up to date.

 - Set up clear policies and processes that scale with the company.

Collaboration

 - Work alongside, supervise and mentor a Junior Legal Counsel, allocating work and reviewing output.

 - Manage external counsel efficiently, including scope and budget, and determine which matters are best handled in-house.

 - Report to the Head of Legal (in the interim, the CFO) and help shape the future structure of the legal team.



Qualifications:

Essential

 - Qualified lawyer with 7+ years' PQE in commercial and corporate law, from a leading firm and/or in-house.

 - Substantial in-house experience in tech, semiconductors, hardware or deep tech, ideally at a scale-up.

 - A strong track record negotiating complex, high-value international contracts, including IP-heavy and supply chain deals.

 - Hands-on use of AI tools in daily legal work, plus experience building playbooks and processes that let a small team scale.

 - Commercial judgement that finds the route to yes, and the ability to explain risk simply to senior stakeholders.

 - Comfort with ambiguity, high volume and shifting priorities.

 - Fluent business English, our working and contract language.

Desirable

 - Semiconductor, AI or embedded systems experience (foundry, licensing, OEM deals).

 - Knowledge of export controls (EU dual-use, US EAR), sanctions and the EU AI Act.

 - Experience implementing CLM or AI contract tools, prompting, or building no-code automations.

 - Experience mentoring junior lawyers, or exposure to venture-backed companies and governance.

 - Dutch or another European language.



How We Work: AI-First Legal
We're building a lean legal function, not scaling by headcount. AI handles first-pass review, redlining, drafting and research, while lawyers focus on judgement and negotiation. Routine work is self-serve through templates and AI-assisted workflows. We measure turnaround and outcomes, and we use AI responsibly, with human review and clear guardrails on confidentiality and accuracy.



Location
Hybrid, with 2 days per week in our Amsterdam or Eindhoven office.

This is your chance to shape and be part of a dynamic, fast-growing, international organization. We offer an attractive compensation package, including a pension plan, extensive employee insurances and the option to get company shares.   

An open culture that supports creativity and continual innovation is awaiting you. Collaborative ownership and freedom with responsibility is characteristic for the way we act and work as a team.

We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

We’re hiring interns to join us in San Francisco. As an intern at Benchling, you’ll have real ownership from day one—building, scaling, and shaping the systems that power our platform and products. Depending on your interests and background, you’ll join either our platform and infrastructure teams (driving scalability, reliability, and performance) or our product and application teams (delivering high-impact features that advance the future of life sciences R&D). You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and technical leads who are passionate about mentorship and engineering excellence—helping you grow rapidly as you make meaningful contributions to a product used by scientists around the world.




RESPONSIBILITIES

You will own a project end-to-end, from initial design, to prototype, to large-scale rollout. You might:

 - Design and implement backend models and API endpoints for complex scientific workflows.

 - Build and operate rich frontend components and visualizations.

 - Design and build a platform framework or infrastructure tool for other Benchling engineers to use.

ABOUT BLACK FOREST LABS

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.

Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.

Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.




WHY THIS ROLE

FLUX is the model developers want. BFL still has to become the platform they choose. In 2026 that platform is judged by a single question, asked by both humans and the agents acting on their behalf: how fast can I go from idea to a production-shaped call, and how good does it feel along the way?

We're hiring one person to own that answer end-to-end. Not the SDK alone, not the dashboard alone, not the API alone — the whole developer experience, for both the humans building on BFL and the agents building on their behalf. You're the person on the team who breathes DevExp: spotting where the platform is friction for a developer or for an agent, deciding whether the fix lives in the API contract, the SDK, the console, the docs surface, the MCP server, or the onboarding flow — and then shipping it.

You sit inside product engineering. You work shoulder-to-shoulder with the API/platform eng team (think: designing the next API revision), with research as new capabilities land, and with DevRel. Your job is to make BFL the platform that wins on developer experience, the way Stripe won payments and Vercel won frontends.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

 - Own DevExp as a product surface — wherever the bottleneck is, that's where you ship next. One sprint that might be the API contract, the next it's the dashboard onboarding, the next it's an MCP server, the next it's a Python SDK abstraction

 - Partner with platform engineering on API design before it ships, not after — bring the developer-and-agent perspective into the room when the contract is being decided

 - Work with product engineering on the developer-facing surfaces of the dashboard — playground, API keys, usage, request inspectors, webhook debugging — bringing the DevExp lens to features the rest of the team is already shipping

 - Make BFL the best visual AI platform for agents to use. Own the MCP server, skills, agent onboarding paths, and the machine-readable surfaces of the platform. Design the reference patterns and SDK primitives developers reach for when building agentic workflows on FLUX. Stress-test every API and SDK change against "would Claude / GPT / an autonomous agent get this right on the first try?" — and treat agents as a first-class user across the whole product (errors an LLM can recover from, capabilities discoverable without a human reading docs, audit trails that make sense when most of the traffic on an account isn't a person).

 - Own the portfolio of entry points developers and agents reach for — SDKs (Python, TypeScript, more on demand), MCP server, skills, OpenAPI / typed surfaces — and treat them as a portfolio, not a hierarchy. SDKs add composable workflows and sane defaults for async / polling / retries; MCP and skills make BFL trivially usable from any agent loop. DevRel and the Creative Technologist team partner on examples, content, and showcase work on top of these surfaces — you own the surfaces themselves.

 - Partner with the Growth engineer and Product on the developer funnel — signup → first key → first call → first production call → repeat — and own the DevExp fixes for the cliffs they surface

 - Be opinionated. Versioning, error formats, breaking change policy, idempotency, naming — you have takes and you can defend them. The bar is Stripe: an API and SDK so well-designed the docs almost feel unnecessary.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years building software, with meaningful time on developer-facing products — SDKs, APIs, dashboards, consoles, platforms developers actually use

 - Full-stack comfortable. TypeScript / React / Next on the front, Python (and ideally Go or Rust) on the back. You don't need a separate person to wire the two halves of a feature together.

 - Deep instincts on API design — you have opinions about error formats, pagination, async job shapes, breaking changes, and you've lived with the consequences of bad ones

 - Fluent in the 2026 agent stack — MCP, tool use, the major agent runtimes — and you know what breaks when an LLM is the one reading your error message or browsing your API

 - You've shipped developer-facing product that real external developers depend on. Not internal tooling.

 - You ship. This is product engineering, not product management with an IDE open.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Background at a developer platform where DevExp was a top-level metric (Stripe, Vercel, Cloudflare, Modal, Replicate, Resend, Linear, Anthropic platform, etc.)

 - You've built or meaningfully contributed to an MCP server real users / agents rely on

 - Experience with media-generation or other high-latency, async, job-shaped APIs — and the UX puzzles that come with them (polling, webhooks, partial results, cost surprises)

 - A public surface — OSS, a writeup, a dashboard you're proud of — that lets us see your taste before the interview

INTRODUCTION

Hi, I'm Al https://www.linkedin.com/in/al-stolz/ and I lead everything customer-facing at Candid. As a team, we’re primarily responsible for delivering valuable outcomes with and for our customers. Prior to Candid, I led teams at McKinsey & Co for 5 years, based in both NYC and Sydney, Australia. I started my career as an M&A lawyer at Allens, a top Australian law firm.

We’re hiring for outstanding folks on my team, and I want to share a bit about how we think about this role, because it's different from what you'll find at most companies - and that difference is very intentional.

At Candid, our model is one where a single, empowered individual is responsible for delivering outcomes with and for customers. Our internal name for this role is “Valkyrie” and it was designed this way from the start. In the early days of Candid, as with many startups, it was impossible to have separate people owning all the things required to help customers win; one person had to integrate across all of it. However, we believe that this isn’t just a startup constraint - it is an incredibly effective way to organize ourselves to win, together with our customers. A single, empowered owner who can move fluidly across functional boundaries will outperform a team of specialists nearly every time, especially in a domain as operationally complex and fragmented as revenue cycle management.

As we've scaled to 200 people and beyond, we've intentionally preserved that model. We've split off certain functionally specialized supporting teams - such as Customer Experience, Forward Deployed Engineering, and Training & Enablement - but the Valkyrie remains the single-point owner of customer outcomes. The anti-pattern we actively resist is the substance-light CSM role that's mostly about relationship management and renewal motions.

To be effective at Candid, you have to be willing and able to operate at the lowest tactical level; iterating on prompts for agent phone calls to navigate payer IVRs, debugging detailed syntax errors in EDI rejections with a clearinghouse, mapping hundreds of fields between a legacy system and ours. Some might describe that work as unglamorous, but the best people on this team relish doing it, because that's where the valuable outcomes live.

But that’s not enough: you also have to be able to zoom out to shape the strategic direction of our partnership with a customer, decomposing complex and ambiguous problems, defining solutions, then driving cross-functional execution to deliver the outcome.  Being able to do both is what really unlocks value for our customers and enables people to thrive in this role.

The shape of person we have seen most commonly thrive in this setting is a low-ego, high-slope generalist. They are resourceful, laser-focused on value delivery, and wired to expand into unowned space rather than wait for scope to be handed to them. This is not a role where your responsibilities are neatly defined and bounded. Valkyries see what needs to happen and make it happen, often before anyone asks. When you spot a gap between teams, an unowned customer problem, or an emerging product opportunity, the expectation is that you move toward it.

Our core thesis - that a scrappy, resourceful generalist given space and expansive ownership will outperform a specialist - has paid off at every stage of Candid's growth. I'm looking for people who will keep proving it right.




THE ROLE

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - As a Valkyrie, you'll be the single owner of outcomes for your customers. Your goal is to help ensure a higher portion of their claims get paid, more quickly, and with less effort. When something stands in the way, it's yours to solve, whether or not it sits neatly in your lane.

 - As part of this, you’ll own the customer relationship at all levels - whether that is the CEO, or the front-line user. You need to be able to flex your engagement style to suit the person, and help tell a compelling value narrative to each persona. As part of this, you’ll go onsite to sit desk-side with users, be able to deliver a killer demo, and do workflow discovery and solutioning. Engaging directly with customers is how we win, and this role is the primary interface and owner of the customer relationship.

 - You'll work at both ends of the spectrum. One day that might be iterating on prompts for agent phone calls to navigate payer IVRs, debugging EDI rejections with a clearinghouse, or mapping fields from a legacy system into ours. The next, you're shaping the strategic direction of our partnership with a customer's leadership team. The detailed work is where the valuable outcomes live.

Fixes may be operational (workflow (re-)design), technical, or product-oriented (automation of manual workflows). You'll bring data-informed recommendations, not just escalations.

 - You'll move toward gaps: between teams, unowned customer problems, emerging product opportunities. You'll pick them up, often before anyone asks, and your scope will grow as fast as you can handle it.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You have a demonstrated track record of expansively owning and driving key business outcomes, ideally by taking on scope no one handed you.

 - You're a low-ego, resourceful generalist. You learn fast, you'll happily do the unglamorous work yourself, and you care more about the customer winning than who gets the credit.

 - You're comfortable without neatly bounded responsibilities. When you spot a gap or an unowned problem, your instinct is to step in rather than wait or hand it off.

 - You can zoom in and out. You're as comfortable debugging a data mapping or an EDI rejection as you are discussing partnership strategy with a customer executive.

Map what data we have and what’s missing. Ship a first activation funnel and get growth, sales and finance to agree on the definitions. Get the account model live and trusted. Come back with the two or three biggest conversion opportunities and a measurable impact for each.

Trust first: the company uses your metrics without arguing about them. Impact second: experiments read weekly on your model, account scoring feeding sales, and conversion gains you can trace to a decision your analysis drove. ABOUT THE ROLE

You will be Fluidstack's safety authority on the ground — our owner's representative embedded in active major construction projects. That means managing GCs and EPCs directly, owning the high-risk activity review process, and protecting Fluidstack's interests across complex, concurrent construction environments that include heavy civil and data center builds.

Current assignments are in Lubbock and Abernathy, Texas. As those projects complete, you move to the next capital project. Ongoing travel is approximately 50%. You report to the HSE Director and operate with the authority to stop work, issue owner-level directives, and escalate to ownership without friction.

This is not a compliance coordination role. You are in the field, holding major contractors accountable, running HRAs, leading incident investigations, and giving leadership clear visibility into what is actually happening on site.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Own safety on the owner's side

 - Serve as Fluidstack's safety authority on active construction sites — the person GCs and EPCs answer to on HSE matters, not the other way around.

 - Review and approve or reject contractor safety plans, site-specific programs, and high-risk work packages before work starts.

 - Conduct structured site inspections and formal audits of GC, EPC, and subcontractor operations; issue written corrective action notices on behalf of Fluidstack.

 - Stop work when conditions demand it. Manage resumption through verified corrective action. Communicate clearly to site leadership and the HSE Director.

 - Attend construction progress and coordination meetings as Fluidstack's HSE representative; hold contractors to their performance commitments.

 - Manage the safety interface across multi-contractor, multi-EPC project environments — concurrent scope, shared hazard zones, and multi-employer coordination.
   

Lead high-risk activity reviews

 - Own the formal High Risk Activity (HRA) review process for critical work phases: energized electrical systems, critical and engineered lifts, confined space entry, deep excavations, structural steel erection, high work, and hot work in sensitive areas.

 - Review and approve contractor lift plans, rigging studies, shoring designs, confined space programs, and energy control procedures on Fluidstack's behalf.

 - Run pre-construction and phase-gate hazard assessments for major project scopes; verify controls are documented and in place before work begins.

 - Lead pre-task planning sessions for high-consequence activities — ensure JHAs reflect actual field conditions, not just paperwork.

 - Maintain a live project risk register: open hazards, assigned controls, responsible contractor, verification status.
   

Manage GC and EPC safety performance

 - Pre-qualify GC and EPC safety programs through rigorous review of EMR history, TRIR/LTIR trends, written program quality, key personnel, and track record on comparable project types.

 - Track contractor safety performance throughout execution — leading indicators, near-miss rates, inspection findings, CAPA closure rates — and report trends to the HSE Director.

 - Issue formal performance notices, cure letters, and escalation recommendations when GC or EPC safety performance falls below contractual standards.

 - Verify that all contractors conduct required orientations, toolbox talks, task-specific training, and competency checks for their workforce.

 - Feed contractor safety performance data directly into contract management decisions — scope adjustments, payment holds, and formal remedies.



Investigate incidents and manage regulatory exposure

 - Respond to and manage all incidents on assigned sites — near-misses, first-aids, recordables, property damage, and environmental releases — regardless of which contracted party is involved.

 - Lead formal root-cause investigations; produce written reports and present findings and corrective actions to the HSE Director and ownership.

 - Serve as Fluidstack's interface with OSHA and other agencies on assigned projects; manage citation response and abatement in coordination with legal.

 - Maintain OSHA recordkeeping compliance across the project; track TRIR/LTIR by contractor and report to the HSE Director on a regular cadence.



Maintain regulatory compliance

 - Working knowledge of OSHA 29 CFR 1926 (Construction), 29 CFR 1910 (General Industry), and NFPA 70E is a baseline — you apply it, you don't reference it.

 - Ensure site-specific environmental compliance is met: SWPPP, SPCC, waste management, and air quality requirements as applicable to each project.

 - Advise the HSE Director proactively on regulatory obligations ahead of upcoming project phases — not reactively after work starts.



Emergency preparedness

 - Ensure every assigned site has a current, site-specific Emergency Action Plan — evacuation, fire, medical, severe weather, utility strikes, and spill/release.

 - Coordinate drills with GC and EPC teams; debrief findings and drive updates to plans.

 - Act as Fluidstack's incident commander or primary support during actual emergencies on site.
   

Report to the HSE Director

 - Weekly field observation reports, monthly safety dashboards, and post-incident summaries — on time, in writing, without prompting.

 - Translate field conditions into owner-level intelligence: what the risk is, what the contractor is doing, what needs to be directed, and what happens if it isn't.

 - Maintain audit-ready project safety documentation: inspection records, corrective action logs, HRA packages, training verification, and incident files.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

ABOUT GIGS

At Gigs, we're building the operating system for mobile services—a platform that lets tech companies embed global connectivity into their products effortlessly.

Just as Stripe lets any business add a payment button in seconds, Gigs empowers platforms to weave in connectivity—bridging the traditional world of telecom with modern tech. From fintechs launching mobile services to HR platforms offering work phone plans, we automate provisioning and remove telecom complexity.

Our team of around 150 people across the US and Europe, backed by nearly $100 million in funding from Ribbit Capital, Google, and Y Combinator. As one of the fastest-growing tech companies, bringing together early-stage engineers, product builders, and business athletes from companies like Stripe, Airbnb, and Shopify. We’re tackling deep technical and regulatory challenges to make connectivity truly seamless.

If you’re driven by curiosity, creativity, and the chance to shape the future of telecom, we’d love to hear from you.




OUR CORE VALUES

 - Win the user. The user is the ultimate judge of our work. Whatever we build needs to be the best in the market. We obsess over the user’s experience, anticipate their needs, and remove every unnecessary friction. We build products users love, not products we have to explain. Our carrier, our partners, and Gigs can only win when the user wins first.

 - Start from First Principles. We start with the ideal outcome, not the existing solution. We challenge convention, strip away unnecessary complexity, and never mistake precedent for progress. “Always been that way” is a red flag, a path of least resistance. At Gigs, we question why things work the way they do, break problems down to their fundamentals, and build from the ground up.

 - Land the Moonshot. Say the outrageous thing, then show how we get there. We pick the moonshot first and plan backwards from it, recalibrating the route as we learn but never the destination. When the carrier, the partner, or the industry says no, that’s a step toward yes: we find the path, rally the right people around us, and land it.

 - Execute Relentlessly. Speed compounds, so we bias to action. Decisions are everyone’s job, and we back them with data we can defend. We adapt to new information without losing momentum. Unless it breaks the laws of physics, we find a way: we name what we need, get it, and keep moving. We measure ourselves by results delivered. Fast is how we move. The bar is what we hold.

 - Be Exceptional, Never Arrogant. We are tackling hard problems, and hard problems take exceptional people. Each of us answers for our own actions and our own success; the buck stops with us. We demand more of ourselves than of anyone else, and it’s on us to help the people around us rise. We are benevolent to ourselves and to each other, and we expect the same in return. Exceptional people make everyone around them better.

 - Candor is Care. We value truth over comfort and candor over politeness. We challenge ideas, question decisions and give feedback directly. We own our mistakes and address problems head-on. It’s never personal. It’s how we get better. The worst feedback is feedback not given. We deliver feedback with respect, genuine care about the improvement of the Gigster and the team.


THE ROLE

GTM Associates at Gigs are the engine of top of funnel growth - and the starting point for a career in commercial leadership. You'll work closely with our GTM Lead to identify, qualify, and develop pipeline for Gigs in the UK & Ireland.

This isn't a role where you execute a handed to you playbook. You'll help build it - and the best people here grow fast because of it. Our GTM org is lean by design. You'll have real visibility with senior operators from day one, and the commercial decisions you make will matter.

For the right person, this is a rare early stage opportunity at a company that has already proven its model in multiple markets and is now executing fast in the UK & Ireland. 

 

What you will do

 - You'll go after the accounts that matter most. You'll work a focused list of must win UK & Ireland accounts - across fintech & banking, retail, travel, utilities and devices - and your job is to get Gigs in the room with them. Depth over volume: a small number of named accounts, pursued brilliantly.

 - You'll grow into deals fast. You'll start by sourcing and qualifying, and advance on capability, not tenure. Run your accounts well and you'll be leading first conversations within your first few quarters, on a clear path (Shadow → Lead → Own) toward deal ownership.

 - You'll get creative about how we get there. Warm introductions, conferences and events, content, product hooks - the London fintech circuit is dense, and you'll pick the rooms that matter, get us into them, and turn conversations into pipeline.

 - You'll own inbound for the region. You'll respond fast, qualify with discipline, and make confident calls on fit.

 - You'll learn the product deeply and make our playbook better. You'll get to grips with our infrastructure, learn why it matters to each buyer, and feed what you learn back into how we sell.

 - You'll work AI-first. Research, outreach, account mapping - you'll run our top of funnel tooling stack, use AI as a natural part of how you work, and iterate on what performs.

 - What success looks like: At 3 months, you know the product and you're running quality first conversations. At 6 months, we're in rooms with must win accounts through paths we wouldn't have found without you. At 12 months, you're leading conversations independently and working live deals alongside the GTM Lead

What we are looking for

 - You're an exceptional communicator. You make complex ideas simple.

 - You're a self-starter who cares about outcomes. You don't wait for a playbook - you help build one. And you measure yourself on commercial impact, not activity.

 - You're energised by technology. You love the idea of businesses embedding mobile connectivity into their products and you want to sell the infrastructure that makes it possible.

 


WORK AT GIGS

At Gigs, we value in-person collaboration. We believe the best ideas, decisions, and relationships are built when teams spend meaningful time together, and our culture is designed around that belief. At Instructure, we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

Foundry is a new division inside Instructure, built to generate new revenue with AI-built products. We operate as a portfolio of small pods, each charged with one product bet, under tight weekly governance. They operate independently, with dedicated resources, separate from the core business on purpose: different pace, different governance, and different rewards.

Our goal is to generate meaningful revenue within 12 to 18 months, so this isn’t an innovation lab. We’re building scaled businesses that customers pay for and retain well, and we’re measuring ourselves on revenue, not activity.

Instructure reaches roughly half of higher education in the United States, connecting a credential network of more than 13,000 institutions. Pair that distribution and data with a fast-moving team that builds leanly, and you have something no competitor has. That’s the opportunity New Markets exists to take.

How we work

A pod is two people: a Founder and a Builder, both hands on, close to the customer. The bet is deliberate: we invest in agent-developer tooling and tokens, not in headcount. An operating team of growth marketing, revenue operations, sales overlay, and G&A supports every pod, so founders stay on building products.

Every pod inherits an underlying platform with common design, development, and deployment harnesses, so no pod rebuilds the plumbing. Each pod runs through key phases with regular checkpoints where a governing board reviews progress or recommends a pivot or kill.

The rhythm is fast and transparent. Investor-style updates go out weekly. Demos and keep-or-kill checkpoints happen twice a month. Transparency is the operating model.

What you will do

You’re the operational engine behind New Markets’ newest product bets. You’ll own the end-to-end go-to-market lifecycle for pod products, from market sizing and early strategy through launch, performance tracking, and the handoff when a product graduates into the core. When a pod proves customers will pay, you make that motion repeatable and hand it to the full seller base. This is a blank-page job: the playbook doesn’t exist yet, and you’ll write it. The role reports directly to the President, New Markets, with a matrixed dotted line to Instructure’s Go-to-Market Strategy and Operations leadership.

What you’ll own

You own go-to-market operations across the portfolio, and you’re the voice of the New Markets business in the rooms where commercial decisions get made.

In practice, that means you’ll:

 - Own the end-to-end GTM lifecycle for pod products. Carry each product from market sizing and early strategy through launch planning, field execution, and post-launch performance tracking.

 - Shape the go-to-market approach with each pod. Partner with Pod Founders, marketing, and the sales overlay on ideal-customer definition, pricing and packaging input, channel strategy, and competitive positioning.

 - Design the sales motion. Build the coverage models, pipeline processes, forecasting cadences, and rules of engagement for the first seller cohort on each product.

 - Build the reporting backbone. Stand up and maintain the analytics in Salesforce and Excel that track pipeline health, win/loss, attach rates, average contract value, and renewal trends, and turn that data into insight leadership can act on.

 - Run launch readiness. Lead CRM buildout in Salesforce, playbook documentation, tool configuration, and alignment across enablement, marketing, finance, deal desk, and IT.

 - Own the graduation playbook. Define the criteria and the integration motion for products that complete a pod’s journey, so the full seller base can carry and sell the product without a messy handoff.

 - Be the voice of the business. Translate early-stage complexity into clear, data-backed narratives in planning forums, business reviews, and executive sessions, and support annual planning across capacity, quota, incentive design, and growth roadmaps.

What we expect

 - Blank page to operating framework. You go from nothing to a working system without a lot of hand-holding, then improve it as results and field feedback come in.

 - Rigor under ambiguity. You structure messy, early-stage go-to-market problems, build the analytical frame, and land a recommendation you can defend.

 - Accuracy you stand behind. The insights and reporting you put in front of leadership are right, and you own them.

 - Influence without authority. You move product, finance, marketing, and sales toward a shared plan without managing any of them.

What we’re looking for

 - Five or more years in sales operations, revenue operations, or a related go-to-market function.

 - Real experience supporting new-product launches or emerging-business initiatives, where the playbook didn’t exist yet.

 - Three or more years hands-on in Salesforce, building and maintaining reports, dashboards, and data structures.

 - Advanced Excel, comfortable building models, running variance analysis, and turning raw data into decision-ready output.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations. A bachelor’s degree is preferred.

Your first 90 days

 - Month 1. Immerse yourself in the New Markets portfolio, the key stakeholders, and the current go-to-market infrastructure. Understand where each product sits in its lifecycle and find the most pressing operational gaps.

 - Month 3. Establish a clear view of performance across active pods: pipeline health, coverage, and leading indicators. Build or refine the reporting framework in Salesforce and Excel, and set a recurring operating rhythm with product and sales leadership.

 - Month 6. Own and drive the go-to-market motion for at least one pod through a checkpoint. Deliver an integration-readiness recommendation for any product approaching graduation, and present a prioritized roadmap for improving New Markets go-to-market operations to senior leadership.

This role isn’t for everyone

Anti-patterns. You should probably pass if:

 - You need an established playbook and a stable process to operate inside. Here you build the playbook.

 - You’re uncomfortable being measured on the accuracy of your numbers and the clarity of your recommendations.

 - You’d rather own a single, well-defined process than the whole messy go-to-market surface across a portfolio.

 - A predictable, slow-changing scope is what you want. The portfolio shifts as pods move through their checkpoints.

Compensation

Base pay is market-competitive. You’ll be paid fairly against the market for the work, so you’re not taking a pay cut to be here. But the base is the floor, not the prize.

The real value is the upside you drive. As part of the operating team, you share in a cash bonus pool tied to portfolio milestones across pods. Targets are set as pods launch, so you’ll know what the portfolio is running at.

The upside is asymmetric, and it’s earned, not granted. There’s a hard floor: below a threshold level of attainment, milestone payouts don’t trigger at all. Above it, hitting and stretching past your targets pays meaningfully. This is built to be the kind of outcome that changes your trajectory, not a routine bonus. The rewards go to the people who build something customers pay for. They don’t reward effort, tenure, or proximity.

What this means in plain terms. Real ownership. Real accountability. Real upside for the people who build a business, and very little for those who don’t. If that trade excites you, you’re the person we’re looking for. If it worries you, trust that instinct.

  • Customer Demonstrations: Prepare and deliver engaging product demonstrations for customers and partners, primarily remotely and occasionally on-site, in English, German, or Korean.

  • Tailored Product Presentations: Adapt demonstrations to specific customer use cases, building types, and project requirements while explaining design logic, planning regulations, and generated outputs.

  • Architectural Quality Assurance: Test new features and configurators before release, evaluating generated site layouts, floor plans, and building models for architectural plausibility, buildability, and compliance with underlying rules.

  • Issue Identification & Documentation: Identify bugs, inconsistencies, and improvement opportunities, documenting findings with clear reproduction steps, screenshots, and structured feedback.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with planning and algorithm teams to prioritize issues and ensure product improvements reflect real architectural and customer requirements.

  • Product Feedback & Roadmap: Gather insights from customer demonstrations and conversations, translating feedback into actionable recommendations for the product roadmap.

  • Knowledge Management: Develop reusable demonstration scripts, test cases, and shared documentation to improve internal knowledge sharing and product evaluation processes.

  • Key Account Management: Serve as the primary product-side contact for selected strategic customers, building strong relationships with their expansion, planning, and real estate teams.

  • Workflow Analysis: Understand customer processes from initial site assessment through permitting, identifying opportunities to automate, simplify, or connect existing workflows.

  • Technical Requirements Translation: Convert customer workflows and operational needs into concrete software requirements, rules, and parameters for development teams.

  • Implementation & Customer Success: Coordinate product rollouts, support customers through implementation and productive use, and maintain engagement after launch.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate combines formal architectural training with strong communication, analytical, and customer-facing skills. You should understand how buildings are designed and planned, be comfortable discussing technical concepts with software engineers, and have the ability to translate complex customer workflows into practical software requirements.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Architecture.

  • Practical experience in architectural design, building planning, or permitting processes is highly desirable.

  • Fluency in English and German is required, with Korean language proficiency considered a strong advantage.

  • Confidence presenting products and communicating with international customers in multiple languages.

  • Basic understanding of artificial intelligence, algorithms, and programming concepts.

  • Ability to understand rule-based systems, interpret simple scripts or logical structures, and communicate effectively with technical development teams.

  • Familiarity with BIM software such as Revit or Archicad is advantageous.

  • Experience with parametric design tools such as Grasshopper is a plus.

  • Strong understanding of architectural planning workflows and customer decision-making processes.

  • Ability to analyze operational processes, identify inefficiencies, and translate findings into clear software requirements.

  • Previous experience in key account management, consulting, or customer-facing project management is highly valued.

  • A forward-deployed mindset, with the ability to work directly with customers, take ownership of their success, and act as a bridge between customer teams and engineers.

  • Excellent presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and a structured approach to testing and documentation.

  • Willingness to travel occasionally for customer visits and on-site collaboration.

    • Benefits:

  • Fully remote working arrangement, with the flexibility to work from anywhere worldwide.

  • Permanent employment contract.

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Opportunity to work at the intersection of architecture, technology, and software innovation.

  • Direct interaction with international customers, including major retailers and real estate developers.

  • Opportunity to influence product development through direct customer feedback and architectural expertise.

  • Close collaboration with a multidisciplinary team of architects, engineers, and software developers.

  • Short decision-making processes within a small, international team.

  • Opportunity to contribute to innovative solutions that transform building design and planning.

  • Flexible start date, with the possibility to join as soon as possible.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer and leading engineering within the Provider Domain, you will be responsible for technical direction, delivery excellence, and team development. Your main responsibilities will include:

- Engineering Strategy and Delivery

  • Own end-to-end engineering delivery across four to five cross-functional teams.

  • Lead through Engineering Managers and Staff-level Engineers within a deliberately flat organizational structure.

  • Ensure teams deliver reliable, scalable systems that support the daily operations of hundreds of thousands of independent businesses.

  • Establish clear priorities and maintain delivery standards across the engineering organization.

    • - Technical Leadership and Standards

  • Define and implement engineering standards, including architecture decision records, technical proposals, and consistent ways of working.

  • Establish frameworks that support sound architectural decisions and encourage technical excellence.

  • Promote engineering practices that improve collaboration, maintainability, and long-term system quality.

    • - AI Transformation and Innovation

  • Lead the integration of AI tools throughout the engineering lifecycle.

  • Identify opportunities to use AI to improve development workflows, productivity, and delivery efficiency.

  • Define measurable success indicators to evaluate the impact of AI adoption while protecting code quality.

    • - Product and Business Alignment

  • Partner with Product leadership to translate commercial strategy into engineering priorities.

  • Use experimentation, data, and business insights to guide technical decisions.

  • Consider unit economics, conversion funnels, growth mechanics, and the commercial impact of engineering initiatives.

    • - People Leadership and Development

  • Build and develop high-performing engineering teams with strong technical capabilities.

  • Coach Engineering Managers and Staff-level Engineers to lead autonomously and make effective decisions.

  • Foster an environment of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is a commercially minded engineering leader who combines strong technical judgment with experience scaling teams and delivering products in fast-growing technology environments. You should be comfortable navigating ambiguity, establishing structure, and remaining connected to technical execution. Key qualifications include:

  • Significant experience leading multiple engineering squads through Engineering Managers and Staff-level Engineers.

  • Background in a high-growth scale-up, high-transaction marketplace, or SaaS business.

  • Strong product mindset, with an understanding of unit economics, growth mechanics, conversion funnels, and the commercial outcomes of engineering decisions.

  • Proven experience establishing engineering standards and practices, including architecture decision records, technical proposals, and structured decision-making frameworks.

  • Practical experience integrating AI tools into everyday engineering workflows.

  • Ability to measure the impact of AI adoption while maintaining high standards for code quality and engineering reliability.

  • Strong collaboration skills and experience translating business and product strategies into technical roadmaps.

  • Ability to lead effectively in a fast-changing environment, bring clarity to ambiguity, and encourage teams to take ownership.

  • Conversational English proficiency at a minimum, as English is the primary language for company-wide communication.

    • Additional experience that would be advantageous:

  • Experience working with two-sided marketplaces or online booking platforms.

  • Exposure to growth engineering, product experimentation, or data-driven optimization.

  • Experience in B2B SaaS environments operating at scale.

    • Benefits:

  • Remote-first working environment within an internationally distributed organization.

  • Flexibility to work fully remotely or access an office where available, depending on the local market.

  • Opportunity to influence the technical strategy of a large-scale, international platform.

  • Significant leadership responsibility across multiple engineering teams.

  • Opportunity to shape AI adoption and modernize engineering practices.

  • Additional benefits vary by location and will be shared during or after the initial conversation with the talent acquisition team.

  • Candidates must be based in the United Kingdom for this advertised position.

  • Applications and CVs must be submitted in English.

Industrial Plant Reliability & Maintenance Expert, AI Evaluation

• Review simulated industrial plant benchmarks from the perspective of an experienced plant reliability and maintenance professional.

  • Evaluate the realism and technical accuracy of simulated plant environments, equipment configurations, and operating conditions.

  • Assess synthetic sensor-data generation to determine whether it reflects plausible industrial measurements and equipment behavior.

  • Review fault scenarios and maintenance cases, evaluating whether issues are realistically represented and technically diagnosable.

  • Assess condition-monitoring signals, including vibration patterns and bearing or cavitation fault signatures.

  • Determine whether the benchmark's proposed fault diagnoses and ground-truth outcomes are technically defensible.

  • Evaluate maintenance scenarios in terms of realistic operational costs, work orders, spare-parts requirements, and shutdown trade-offs.

  • Use historian data, piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), and maintenance documentation to validate simulated conditions and scenarios.

  • Provide clear, structured feedback and practical recommendations to improve benchmark accuracy and relevance to real industrial operations.

    • Requirements:

  • Typically 10 or more years of hands-on experience in process plants, industrial operations, plant reliability, or maintenance engineering, or equivalent substantial practical expertise.

  • Strong knowledge of rotating equipment and associated systems, including centrifugal pumps, electric motors, suction strainers, and coolers.

  • Practical expertise in condition monitoring, particularly vibration analysis and the identification of bearing and cavitation fault signatures.

  • Ability to interpret industrial historian data and assess equipment performance using operational measurements.

  • Familiarity with piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), maintenance records, and technical plant documentation.

  • Solid understanding of maintenance economics, including work-order processes, spare-parts planning, equipment downtime, and shutdown-related decisions.

  • Ability to evaluate technical scenarios critically and distinguish realistic industrial behavior from inaccurate or overly simplified simulations.

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to communicate technical observations and recommendations in a structured manner.

  • Practical judgment and the ability to apply real-world plant experience to the evaluation of simulated environments and AI-generated scenarios.

    • Benefits:

  • Contract compensation of approximately US$90 per hour.

  • Flexible, fully remote working arrangement.

  • Limited time commitment of approximately 5 hours per week.

  • Initial engagement period of 3 months.

  • Opportunity to apply specialist industrial expertise to the evaluation and development of AI systems.

  • Flexible location, with candidates based in the United States or Europe preferred.

The Information Security Lead will design, implement, and continuously improve the organization's information security framework, taking a pragmatic and automation-driven approach. This position combines hands-on security engineering, risk management, infrastructure protection, and incident oversight, ensuring that security practices remain effective, scalable, and aligned with business priorities.

  • Design and implement identity and access management (IAM) across core business tools and third-party vendors handling customer data, including single sign-on (SSO), enforced passkeys, least-privilege access, and regular access reviews.

  • Coordinate identity and access management initiatives with IT to centralize security controls and improve access governance.

  • Own and maintain the information security risk register, identifying organizational vulnerabilities and working with leadership to prioritize mitigation strategies or formally accept risks.

  • Maintain a comprehensive inventory of externally exposed assets and ensure they are regularly monitored and patched against known vulnerabilities, including CISA alerts and vendor security advisories.

  • Secure cloud and product infrastructure, including AWS accounts, build systems, secrets management, and email security configurations such as DMARC, SPF, and DKIM.

  • Implement endpoint security and software package controls across employee and engineering devices.

  • Organize annual external penetration tests and establish continuous automated security testing between assessments, leveraging AI agents and external services where appropriate.

  • Manage the bug bounty program, including defining its scope, coordinating vulnerability triage, and overseeing payouts, with a focus on meaningful risks such as unauthorized access to personal data.

  • Maintain the security incident log and lead incident analysis from a risk management perspective, coordinating with responsible teams acting as first responders.

  • Conduct incident postmortems, document findings, and ensure appropriate follow-up actions are implemented.

  • Manage relationships with external security providers, penetration testing firms, the Data Protection Officer (DPO), and other security partners.

  • Promote practical security awareness by prioritizing effective technical controls and leveraging existing training solutions rather than building unnecessary internal programs.

  • Ensure compliance evidence is generated through everyday security operations, including access reviews, patching records, and incident documentation, automating evidence collection wherever possible.

  • Deliver key security foundations during the first 90 days, including SSO and enforced passkeys, an initial access review, a leadership-reviewed risk register, an exposed-asset inventory, an operational patching process, and an incident management framework.

  • Establish an implementation roadmap for endpoint and package management, alongside continuous security testing capabilities.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced security engineer with a strong background in product-focused environments and hands-on expertise in securing cloud infrastructure, identities, and software systems. They should combine technical depth with practical risk judgment, automation capabilities, and the ability to communicate security priorities effectively to senior stakeholders and engineering teams.

  • At least 5 years of hands-on experience in security engineering within a product-oriented technology company.

  • Strong identity and access management experience across SaaS platforms and cloud environments, including SSO, multi-factor authentication (MFA), passkeys, and access reviews.

  • Practical experience securing AWS infrastructure, particularly IAM, network controls, and AWS security services.

  • Proven experience managing vulnerabilities and patching processes across externally exposed assets.

  • Strong scripting and automation capabilities using infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform and languages including Python, Bash, or similar.

  • Experience managing security incidents from an analytical and risk ownership perspective, including conducting investigations and writing postmortem reports.

  • Ability to assess and prioritize genuine security risks over theoretical findings, focusing on practical business impact.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain complex security issues to executives and gain alignment across technical teams.

  • Fluent English, both written and spoken, as it is the primary working language within a multicultural environment.

    • Additional Skills Considered a Plus:

  • Previous experience managing or contributing to a bug bounty program.

  • Experience using AI agents for security testing, vulnerability discovery, or operational automation.

  • Knowledge of email security standards and configurations, including DMARC, SPF, and DKIM.

  • Experience implementing endpoint security and Mobile Device Management (MDM) controls.

  • Familiarity with software supply chain security, including package controls, dependency pinning, and signed builds.

  • Understanding of privacy and regulatory requirements affecting children's digital products, particularly COPPA, GDPR-K, and KidSAFE.

  • Relevant professional certifications such as AWS Security Specialty, CISSP, or OSCP.

    • Benefits:

  • Annual gross salary ranging from €60,000 to €70,000, depending on experience and qualifications.

  • Equity participation in addition to base compensation.

  • Potential consideration for a more senior position with a corresponding compensation range for candidates bringing significantly greater experience.

  • Fully remote working arrangement within Spain.

  • Full-time employment opportunity.

  • Significant ownership and autonomy to build and manage the organization's information security function.

  • Opportunity to work with modern cloud technologies, automation tools, and AI-powered security solutions.

  • Direct collaboration with senior leadership and cross-functional engineering teams.

  • Opportunity to protect sensitive information and build trust for a digital platform serving millions of families.

  • Inclusive and diverse working environment that values different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences.

  • Employment governed by the applicable Spanish collective bargaining agreement for consulting, IT, and market research companies.

Líder de Machine Learning, Data Science e IA

You will define and execute the machine learning and AI strategy, establish the technical foundations for production-ready models, and lead the development of intelligent solutions that improve operational efficiency, risk management, and financial decision-making.

  • Define the machine learning and AI roadmap, prioritizing use cases in collaboration with Product, Compliance, and Finance teams.

  • Build and develop the organization's model platform on Databricks, including feature engineering, model training, model registries, real-time serving, and performance monitoring.

  • Ensure the scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency of machine learning infrastructure and production environments.

  • Lead the development and deployment of initial models, focusing on transactional fraud detection, anti-money laundering (AML) risk scoring, and credit origination for new financial products.

  • Transform transactional data from SPEI, direct debit, bill payments, and cross-border operations into actionable insights and production-ready models.

  • Lead generative AI and agent-based initiatives, including specification-driven development (SDD), agentic onboarding, customer support automation, and Second Brain solutions.

  • Establish evaluation frameworks and standards for generative AI applications, with particular attention to cost management, performance, and sensitive data protection.

  • Implement model governance frameworks covering explainability, traceability, documentation, and regulatory readiness.

  • Ensure that machine learning solutions meet applicable regulatory requirements and audit standards, including those established by CNBV and Banxico.

  • Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to communicate model performance, explain technical decisions, and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Recruit, develop, and lead the first four members of the machine learning and data science team within the first 12 months.

  • Build a high-performing team and establish the processes, standards, and technical practices required for sustainable AI development.

You should combine deep technical expertise with leadership capabilities, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate complex analytical concepts into practical business and regulatory decisions.

  • At least 7 years of experience in machine learning, with demonstrated success deploying models at scale.

  • Experience developing and managing models in high-concurrency environments requiring real-time inference.

  • Work Management.

  • Maintenance Planning and Scheduling.

  • Preventive and Corrective Maintenance.

  • Fuel and Driver Management.

  • Inventory and Materials Management.

  • Purchasing and Procurement.

  • Warranty and Contract Management.

  • Labor, Crew, and Resource Management.

  • Mentor client teams and share functional knowledge to strengthen internal capabilities.

  • Contribute to successful delivery across geographically distributed teams and international project environments.

    • Requirements:

    You are an experienced IBM Maximo professional with specialized knowledge of transportation asset management and enterprise implementation projects.   • Bring at least 3 years of specific experience with Maximo for Transportation implementations or solutions.

  • Demonstrate solid expertise in system configuration, setup, functional design, and optimization.

  • Have a strong understanding of transportation asset management processes and operational requirements.

• Architect, design, and validate mechanical components, mechanisms, electromechanical assemblies, and electronic board and enclosure layouts for advanced embedded systems.
  • Develop detailed, production-ready mechanical designs, including engineering drawings, bills of materials (BOMs), geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), and tolerance stack-up analyses.
  • Conduct and oversee mechanical and thermal design validation through laboratory testing, including thermal, vibration, and mechanical performance assessments.
  • Collaborate with electronic hardware engineers and PCB layout designers to translate client specifications and technical requirements into conceptual and detailed mechanical solutions.
  • Support presales activities by reviewing requests for quotations (RFQs) and requests for proposals (RFPs), defining project scope, assessing technical requirements, and preparing effort estimates in collaboration with clients and estimating teams.
  • Coordinate with project managers and external mechanical and thermal engineering partners to review estimates, establish priorities, monitor schedules, and ensure deliverables meet agreed timelines and budgets.
  • Provide technical and quality oversight of mechanical designs, thermal engineering, and finite element analysis (FEA) activities across internal teams and external partners.
  • Evaluate design quality, identify technical or operational risks, and proactively address scope, schedule, and delivery issues.
  • Serve as the primary mechanical and thermal engineering point of contact for assigned client engagements, ensuring alignment between mechanical, electrical, and thermal design activities.
  • Manage relationships with external design, engineering, and manufacturing partners, reviewing quotations, negotiating delivery schedules, and ensuring quality standards are consistently achieved.
  • Collaborate with electronic design automation (EDA) tool suppliers to assess and implement tools that meet evolving mechanical and thermal engineering requirements.
  • Identify and champion the adoption of AI-powered tools and emerging technologies to improve engineering workflows, design productivity, and operational efficiency.
  • Support resource planning and project staffing by identifying the mechanical and thermal expertise required for new engagements.
  • Mentor and support colleagues through technical guidance, hands-on training, knowledge sharing, and professional development.
  • Contribute to cross-functional engineering initiatives involving FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, signal integrity, power integrity, and PCB design.
  • Travel domestically and internationally when required to support client engagements, technical discussions, and project delivery.

    • Requirements:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or an equivalent technical qualification.
  • At least 10 years of professional experience designing mechanical components and systems for electronic assemblies, including senior-level or technical leadership responsibilities.
  • Strong proficiency in at least one major mechanical CAD platform, such as SolidWorks, Creo, Siemens NX, or Autodesk Inventor.
  • Working knowledge of thermal engineering and finite element analysis (FEA) principles, including tools such as FloTHERM, ANSYS Icepak, or equivalent, with the ability to review, evaluate, and guide the work of other specialists.
  • Practical experience with rapid prototyping techniques, including 3D printing, CNC machining, and sheet metal fabrication, to support proof-of-concept development and design validation.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing laboratory testing, including thermal, vibration, and mechanical testing, to verify product performance against technical specifications.
  • Proven ability to manage external engineering, design, thermal analysis, and manufacturing partners, including evaluating quotations, negotiating schedules, and monitoring quality and delivery performance.
  • Strong client-facing experience, with the ability to present technical designs, communicate project progress, resolve engineering challenges, and contribute to RFQ/RFP and project scoping discussions.
  • Comprehensive understanding of engineering materials, mechanical assemblies, manufacturing processes, and production methods, including machining, sheet metal fabrication, injection molding, and die casting.
  • Solid understanding of electronic cooling principles, heat transfer, and thermal management fundamentals for complex electronic systems.
  • Expertise in preparing detailed mechanical documentation suitable for prototyping and manufacturing, including engineering drawings, GD&T, and tolerance stack-up analysis.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent client projects, balance competing priorities, and maintain high standards of technical quality and delivery.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered engineering and mechanical design tools, combined with an interest in integrating emerging technologies to improve productivity, efficiency, and design processes.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams and communicate complex technical concepts clearly.
  • Willingness and availability to travel within Canada and internationally when required.
  • Ability to successfully complete applicable background checks and security screening under Canada's Controlled Goods Program (CGP). Depending on project requirements, eligibility to obtain security clearance under the Contract Security Program (CSP), administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada, may also be necessary.
  • Professional integrity, strong problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to technical leadership and continuous improvement.

• Conduct field inspections of mechanical and welded installations, including structural steel, chilled water and hydronic piping, process piping, and associated supports, ensuring compliance with technical drawings, specifications, approved submittals, and applicable industry codes.
  • Review and validate Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS), Procedure Qualification Records (PQR), and Welder Performance Qualifications (WPQ) before welding activities begin.
  • Maintain accurate welder qualification logs for each assigned project site.
  • Perform visual weld inspections before, during, and after welding activities, verifying fit-up, preheating, welding consumables, workmanship, and final weld profiles.
  • Coordinate third-party nondestructive examinations (NDE), including Magnetic Particle Testing (MT), Penetrant Testing (PT), Ultrasonic Testing (UT), and Radiographic Testing (RT), and verify results against applicable acceptance criteria.
  • Witness and document hydrostatic and pneumatic pressure tests, as well as piping flushing and cleaning activities, before insulation and final system turnover.
  • Inspect mechanical equipment installations, including chillers, Computer Room Air Handler (CRAH) and Computer Room Air Conditioner (CRAC) units, pumps, cooling towers, and air handling units, verifying positioning, alignment, anchorage, and connections.
  • Execute mechanical and welding inspection requirements outlined in project Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), supporting the QA/QC Manager in identifying and managing inspection hold points and witness points.
  • Identify workmanship deficiencies, issue or initiate Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and verify corrective actions before work is approved to proceed.
  • Verify material traceability and documentation, including Mill Test Reports (MTRs), heat numbers, and material certifications for piping, fittings, and structural steel.
  • Maintain comprehensive inspection records, weld maps, test reports, and quality documentation to support commissioning activities and final project handover.
  • Work closely with construction teams, trade contractors, and project leadership to communicate quality concerns, resolve technical issues, and maintain project standards.
  • Identify potential installation and quality risks early, helping prevent rework, operational failures, and delays during commissioning.
  • Travel to assigned project locations and provide consistent on-site quality oversight throughout each project assignment.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 5 years of professional experience in mechanical and/or welding inspection within commercial, industrial, or mission-critical construction environments.
  • Current AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) or Certified Pipe Welding Inspector (CPWI) certification.
  • Working knowledge of applicable industry standards and codes, including AWS D1.1, ASME B31.9 and/or B31.3, and ASME Section IX.
  • Demonstrated experience reviewing WPS, PQR, and WPQ documentation and validating welder qualifications in active construction environments.
  • Hands-on experience conducting visual weld inspections and evaluating mechanical installation quality.
  • Experience witnessing, documenting, and verifying hydrostatic and pneumatic pressure testing of piping systems.
  • Ability to interpret mechanical and structural drawings, piping isometrics, Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), technical specifications, and welding symbols.
  • Experience identifying construction deficiencies, managing quality documentation, and preparing or tracking Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
  • Understanding of material traceability requirements, including material certifications, mill test reports, and heat number verification.
  • Strong knowledge of mechanical equipment installation, piping systems, welding practices, and construction quality control procedures.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare detailed inspection reports and communicate technical deficiencies clearly to contractors and project leadership.
  • Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently in demanding construction environments, exercise sound technical judgment, and address quality issues proactively.
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively and work on-site for extended assignments, typically lasting 3–6 months.
  • NACE Coating Inspector Level 1 or Level 2 certification is considered an advantage.
  • Additional certifications such as ASNT Level II in MT, PT, UT, or RT, API 570, API 510, or ICC credentials are highly desirable.
  • Previous inspection experience on data center, hyperscale, or other mission-critical construction projects is a strong advantage.
  • Familiarity with Procore or equivalent construction management and quality tracking platforms is preferred.
  • Understanding of commissioning (Cx) processes and the relationship between installation quality and functional performance testing is beneficial.
  • Experience in related industries such as oil and gas, LNG, power generation, or industrial process facilities is an added advantage.
  • A proactive, adaptable, and results-oriented mindset, with the ability to work effectively in fast-paced environments and take ownership of quality outcomes.

    • Benefits:

  • Subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Equity participation through stock options in a rapidly growing technology and infrastructure company.
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with a 4% employer match.
  • Unlimited paid time off (PTO).
  • Parental leave.
  • Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) or Health Savings Account (HSA).
  • Commuter benefits.
  • Monthly in-person team gatherings and company-wide collaboration events.
  • Opportunity to contribute to large-scale data center and mission-critical infrastructure projects.
  • Hands-on experience in a rapidly expanding industry supporting the growth of AI infrastructure.
  • Collaborative, high-performance environment offering significant ownership and professional development opportunities.
