ABOUT PEEC AI

AI search is changing how brands are discovered and chosen. People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Google’s AI answers what they used to search for, and AI assistants increasingly shape the journey from discovery to purchase. Winning customers now means winning over the AI systems that influence their decisions.

Peec AI is an AI search platform that helps marketing teams understand and improve how their brands are discovered, represented, and recommended. We show them where they stand, what’s shaping it, and where to act. Since launching in January 2025, Peec AI has passed $20M ARR and 4,000+ paying customers. We’re a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, with 100+ people across our Berlin HQ and our New York office.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Peec ships something new almost every week. Most customers hear about it late, and some never do. We're hiring a Customer Education Manager to own how customers learn Peec. You'll own the product docs, the changelog, product updates and in-app communication, and turn every release into something a busy marketer understands in a minute.

You'll sit in product marketing and report to our founding product marketer. You'll work every day with product managers and engineers to understand what's shipping, with customer success to see where customers get stuck, and with the growth team to see what actually changes how people use the product.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product docs. Rebuild them around the jobs customers come to do, not around the menu. Keep them current with every release, and make them easy to read for people and for the AI assistants our customers now ask first.

 - Run the changelog and product updates. Every release gets a clear entry the day it ships. You write the regular product update and the announcement for bigger launches, and decide what deserves which.

 - Write in-app communication. You write the copy for announcements, tooltips, empty states, onboarding steps and feature nudges. The growth team runs the nudges themselves (who sees what, when, and the tests); you make sure every message is clear, accurate and sounds like one product.

 - Make product content that teaches. Short how-to videos, walkthroughs, use-case guides and templates that get a new user from signup to their first useful insight, and an existing customer to the feature they're missing.

 - Get in early. Sit with product and engineering before launch, early enough to shape naming, setup and the first-run experience, not just document them afterwards.

 - Fix questions at the source. Read support tickets and customer calls, find the questions we keep answering, and make sure the product, docs or messaging answer them before anyone has to ask.

 - Measure what you ship. Track docs usage, support deflection and feature adoption after each update. Keep what works, cut what doesn't.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You come from product. Product management, product ops, technical writing, solutions or support engineering, or customer success with a strong product bent. You learn software deeply by using it and can get a straight answer from a busy engineer.

 - You've owned docs, a help center or release communication for a B2B SaaS product. Show us a before and after.

 - You write simply. You can explain a complex feature in three sentences to someone who has never seen it, and cut a page in half without losing anything. We'll ask for recent work where your part is clear.

 - You like to ship a lot. Many small, useful pieces over one perfect one, and you care as much about keeping them up to date as about publishing them.

 - You're comfortable with data. Given adoption numbers, you can say whether a piece of content worked.

 - You use AI to draft, research and keep content in sync with the product. You build the systems that other teams can plug into to ensure consistency across every touchpoint.

 - You work well across product, engineering, customer success and marketing, make decisions and ship.




BONUS POINTS

 - You built a docs or customer education function from scratch, first in seat.

 - You've worked in martech, SEO, analytics or a data platform, so you already know our customers' world.

 - You make short product videos and screen recordings yourself.

 - You've written in-app messages or product emails in tools like Customer.io http://Customer.io, Intercom, Appcues or Pendo.

 - You know how to structure docs so AI assistants read and cite them correctly.

 - You write well in German or French as well as English.

At Proxima Fusion, we are building the future of clean energy - and we need an experienced Warehouse Specialist who thrives in a fast-paced, hands-on environment. In this role, you will ensure the smooth and efficient flow of materials and equipment, supporting our engineering, R&D, and operational ambitions. You’ll be responsible for managing incoming and outgoing goods, maintaining accurate inventory records, coordinating shipments, and ensuring the safe handling and storage of materials. With a strong focus on reliability, precision, and continuous improvement, you’ll play a key role in building efficient and scalable warehouse operations that support our mission to make fusion energy a reality.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Goods receipt and inspection: Receive deliveries from suppliers, carriers and couriers. Check each one against the purchase order and delivery note for quantity, part number and condition. Look for transport damage, moisture, contamination or tampering. Verify labels, batch and serial numbers, and shelf life.

 - Non-conformance and claims: Photograph and document any findings. Move non-conforming goods to blocked or quarantine stock and raise non-conformance reports. File claims with carriers, inform Purchasing, and hand parts that need detailed inspection to Quality. Release or return them based on Quality’s decision.

 - System accuracy (ERP/WMS): Post goods receipts and goods issues accurately and on time, including labels, barcodes, and batch and serial numbers. Book goods in only after they pass the receipt checks. Keep physical stock and system stock in sync.

 - Dispatch and shipping documents: Pick, pack and prepare shipments according to packing instructions. Create delivery notes, labels, CMR consignment notes and packing lists. For non-EU shipments, prepare proforma invoices and export documents with the logistics team. Prepare ADR transport documents for hazardous goods.

 - Carrier coordination and returns: Book and coordinate pickups, and track shipments until they’re delivered. Handle returns and re-shipments to suppliers through the RMA process.

 - Loading, unloading and transport: Load and unload trucks and vans safely with forklifts and pallet jacks, and secure loads correctly. Handle heavy, bulky, sensitive or high-value components with care. Run scheduled milk runs between company sites and local suppliers using company vehicles.

 - Storage, replenishment and inventory: Sort, label and store goods in the correct locations. Replenish production and line-side stock (Kanban or min/max) in time for manufacturing. Take part in the annual stocktake and resolve stock differences. Manage packaging materials: stock levels, reordering, reuse and recycling.

 - Housekeeping and safety: Keep receiving, storage and dispatch areas clean and organised with a 5S mindset. Separate and dispose of waste according to German recycling rules. Follow health and safety rules and wear PPE. Report hazards, near-misses and accidents, and carry out daily checks on forklifts and handling equipment.

 - Cross-functional coordination: Work with Purchasing, Production, Quality, Engineering and Finance on material availability, priorities and urgent shipments, and keep internal customers informed.

 - Continuous improvement and travel: Suggest and support improvements to warehouse processes, layout and digital tools. Travel within the EU when needed, for example to suppliers, partner sites or with special shipments.



WHO YOU ARE

 - Completed vocational training as Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik, Fachlagerist/in or a comparable qualification, or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - At least 5 years of experience in goods receipt, dispatch or warehousing, ideally in a manufacturing environment.

 - Valid EU/German driving licence, class B.

 - Valid forklift licence (Staplerschein per DGUV Grundsatz 308-001) and confident operation of counterbalance forklifts.

 - Fluent German and English, spoken and written (at least B2 in both).

 - Tech-savvy: confident with ERP/WMS systems (e.g. SAP or similar), barcode scanners, Google Workspace, and email.

 - Good knowledge of shipping documents and processes (delivery notes, CMR, Incoterms basics).

 - Knowledge of load securing and safe handling of goods.

 - Willingness to travel within the EU when required.

Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running. We value restless curiosity, creative thinking, and diverse perspectives as we strive to become AI-native. We believe that AI is a collaborator, not just a tool, and we invite passionate individuals to join us on our journey as we continue to learn, experiment, and grow together.



We're hiring a Senior SRE to help us run and evolve the infrastructure behind Signal AI's decision intelligence platform.



You'd be joining a small, collaborative Infrastructure team at a moment when the work is genuinely changing shape. Over the last year, we've hardened the platform, reduced cost, and built serious observability into our highest-volume systems. The next year is about scaling that work, absorbing infrastructure from a recent acquisition, and being thoughtful about how AI shows up in operational work: not as a gimmick, but as a tool we trust ourselves to use well.



We're looking for someone who wants to shape the team's direction; someone people can rely on for tricky or urgent problems; someone who brings curiosity and care to the work; and someone who wants to leave things meaningfully better than they found them.




WHAT WE'VE SHIPPED RECENTLY

 - Cut ~$50k/year off our Elasticsearch bill by migrating compute to more efficient chips. (Apr 2026)

 - Built the foundation for our MCP server platform: leveraging and contributing to open-source tooling to give the whole company extensible, production-grade AI integrations. (2025–2026)

 - Rebuilt production from scratch in a full DR game day. End-to-end restore validated across our multi-account AWS setup. (Jan 2026)


WHAT WE'RE WORKING ON NEXT

 - AI-augmented operations: Claude Enterprise is deployed across Signal. We want this team to help define what good looks like for SRE: incident triage, runbook generation, capacity planning, cost analysis. This is a strategic investment, not a side project, and we'd love someone genuinely curious about what these tools can and can't do.

 - Security in the age of AI: The threat landscape has shifted. Supply chain security is more at threat than ever, and powerful models are emerging that promise to change how the industry thinks about security. We're looking for someone interested in thinking seriously about what actually matters to protect now.

 - Acquisition integration: Bringing a recently acquired product's infrastructure under our reliability, security, and operational standards. A substantial, multi-quarter piece of work with real technical and organisational complexity, and plenty of room to make your mark.

 - Batch workload consolidation: Moving disparate batch jobs onto EKS for unified scheduling, cost visibility, and operational tooling.




YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

We want to set you up to thrive. Here's what that looks like in practice:

 - Month 1: You're onboarded across our AWS estate, Terraform, and observability stack. You've completed your first on-call shift with team support, landed your first PR in the DevOps repo, and started working Claude Enterprise into your daily flow.

 - Month 3: You're owning a workstream end-to-end. You've led the SRE response to at least one production incident and hosted your first post-mortem. You've surfaced a real opportunity and pushed it to a measurable result.

 - Month 6: You're driving a multi-quarter workstream with clear direction, coaching less experienced teammates along the way, and contributing insights to our AI-in-operations playbook: including where Claude adds real leverage and where it doesn't.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have solid AWS and Terraform experience, and you're comfortable writing Python or Go to solve operational problems. You think in distributed systems: failure modes, observability, blast radius: and you take problems end-to-end rather than stopping at the edges of your own work.



When a problem is complex, you can lay out a few ways to solve it, weigh the trade-offs, and recommend the one that meets our needs now without sacrificing tomorrow. You take personal ownership of customer-impacting issues in the systems you look after.



You communicate openly and you're comfortable pushing back when you think something could be better. You give clear, actionable feedback and you enjoy helping others level up.



You're pragmatic about AI tooling. Not evangelical, not dismissive. You can tell us when you'd reach for an LLM and when you wouldn't, and you'd have a clear reason either way.



We know not every strong candidate will have every skill on this list. If you're excited about the work and you're close on the experience, we'd encourage you to apply.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Networking depth. You're comfortable below the load balancer: TCP/IP fundamentals, DNS, VPC design, and what actually happens when a service can't reach another one.

 - Operational security instincts. You follow the threat landscape with genuine interest: not just CVEs, but shifts in how attacks happen and how the industry is responding. You have a point of view on what actually matters right now.

 - Linux internals comfort. When something behaves strangely under load, you know where to look.

 - Elasticsearch at scale. Sharding, index lifecycle management, node failures and JVM tuning.

 - Communication across technical levels. You can collaborate with your infrastructure teammates and explain the same concepts clearly to a product manager.

Not sure you meet every requirement? Studies show that women and other underrepresented groups often hesitate to apply unless they check every box. At Signal AI, diverse perspectives strengthen our teams, drive innovation, and lead to better performance. So even if your background doesn’t align perfectly with each qualification, we encourage you to apply if you’re passionate about this role.

We're dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where every Signaller feels welcomed, valued, and heard—a place where you can truly thrive as yourself.

Skyflow secures the flow of data across datastores, models, and agents. Enterprises turn to Skyflow as their runtime AI data control layer to protect sensitive data, enable safe AI deployment, and unlock full value from their applications, data platforms, and AI systems. 

Skyflow is trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises, and leading SaaS companies in financial services, healthcare, retail, travel and hospitality.



Skyflow is headquartered in Palo Alto, California and was founded in 2019. For more information, visit www.skyflow.com http://www.skyflow.com or follow on X https://twitter.com/SkyflowAPI and LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/skyflow/.

 


ABOUT SKYFLOW



Skyflow is a data privacy vault: a platform that businesses use to store, protect, and use their most sensitive and regulated data. Our customers trust us with personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), and payment card data (PCI). They use tokenization, field-level encryption, and fine-grained access control so their own systems never have to touch raw sensitive data.

That makes security our product, not just a function that supports it. A security event at Skyflow can become a security event for every customer who relies on us. Customers' auditors and regulators depend on our controls. We are moving into larger enterprises and regulated industries, and they expect service-provider security to meet a higher standard, especially as AI-accelerated attacks shorten the time between a weakness and its exploitation.






ABOUT THE ROLE



You will be the primary owner of Skyflow's existing security operations, taking a capable function to the next level as we serve larger enterprises. This is a broad role. It spans detection and response and the operational work behind our controls: vulnerability remediation, credential and key rotation, access minimization, and automated evidence.

You will lead from day one: directing our SOC analysts and specialist partners, and stepping in personally on the highest-stakes incidents. As Skyflow scales, you will advance the operation by setting direction for the right tooling, automation, and AI agents, and holding their output to a high bar. You'll give analysts, engineering teams, and AI tools clear, detailed direction: the runbooks, detection standards, and playbooks they execute.

You'll work closely with Application Security, Infrastructure Security, Compliance, and Corp Security. You will also partner with Engineering and SRE, and you'll face customers during security reviews and incident communications.






YOU HAVE:



 - 10+ years in security, including 4+ years leading security operations, detection and response, or SOC teams.

 - Deep detection and incident response expertise: you can judge the quality of a detection or an investigation, and command a high-severity incident.

 - Experience securing SaaS platforms that handle regulated data such as payments, healthcare, or financial services, under PCI DSS and SOC 2 programs.

 - Deep AWS security experience, with GCP a plus: IAM, KMS, GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, VPC, and WAF. Strong working knowledge of Kubernetes and container security.

 - Practical experience with SIEM, EDR, and SOAR tools, and with MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF.

 - A track record of maturing security procedures through automation, such as credential rotation, access reviews, and evidence collection.

 - Enough technical depth in Python or Go, Terraform, CI/CD, and detection-as-code to direct and review the work.

 - An AI-first mindset: you direct AI tools daily, evaluate their output critically, and have built security operations largely through tooling and automation.

 - Clear communication with engineers, executives, customers, and auditors, including in the middle of an incident.






NICE TO HAVE:



 - Experience at a security, data protection, payments, or infrastructure company where security is part of the product.

 - Familiarity with tokenization, encryption, HSM- and KMS-backed key management, or privacy-enhancing technologies.

 - Experience with HIPAA, ISO 27701, HITRUST, or FedRAMP readiness.

 - Experience building or leading distributed SOC teams across the US and India, or managing an MDR partner.

 - Experience securing AI agents, LLM applications, or MCP integrations.

Build Trust

Deliver Results

 - Customer Onboarding and Adoption: Own onboarding and early adoption end-to-end, and design tailored enablement and custom onboarding assets using AI coding agents.

Grow Trust

 - Articulating and Proving Value: Connect platform features to business outcomes through a consumption and adoption lens, and prepare business reviews, consumption health checks and value realisation reports.

 - Driving Growth and Expansion: Partner with the Account Executive to identify and drive expansion in your accounts, and lead the creation and progression of new use cases.

Collaboration and Community

 - Enablement: Design and deliver customer workshops, enablement sessions and office hours.

 - Knowledge Sharing: Replicate successful activation strategies and share AI-native workflows with the wider team.

 - Operational Excellence: Keep account and use case data accurate, and self-audit records before reviews.

 - Certification: SnowPro Core certification.

 - Education: A degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - SnowPro Advanced certification.

 - Programming experience in Python, Java or Scala, and experience with dbt, CI/CD and orchestration tools.

 - Daily use of AI-powered development tools and coding agents to accelerate delivery.

 - Experience leading customer workshops or enablement sessions.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join Supabase’s Interfaces group and help run the backend services behind our developer tools, starting with postgres-meta: the open-source service that runs SQL against customers’ Postgres databases on behalf of our dashboard, our MCP server, AI agents, and other platform tools. You’ll work closely with the engineers who build those tools, and with our Platform and SRE teams.

AI agents are the fastest-growing source of postgres-meta’s traffic, and it sits on the path between developers and their data, so when it struggles, people can’t reach their databases from the dashboard or their agents. The team’s first priority is making it reliable, observable, and fair between tenants at agent scale, and helping redesign it for that scale without breaking the tools that depend on it. Depending on your experience, you’ll own major parts of that work or lead it. Alongside it, the team builds the backend services that give every branch of a project the configuration and secrets it needs.

We want to be upfront: this role carries real operational load. Our on-call process and rotation are new and need a lot of maturing, and you’ll help build them into something sustainable from your first weeks. You’ll be on call for services on the critical path, and incidents come before planned work. Platform teams run the infrastructure underneath; you’ll own the services themselves, from their code to how they behave in production. It’s ideal for someone who enjoys that kind of ownership, thrives in async, fast-paced environments, and stays calm when the root cause turns out to be in someone else’s system.



WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

In this role, you’ll:

 - Help mature the team’s on-call from your first weeks: grow the rotation to cover every service the team runs, write runbooks, and agree when to declare an incident. Then build it, with our embedded SRE, into a sustainable follow-the-sun rotation as the team grows.

 - Set SLOs with the teams that call the service, and build the observability to hold them: metrics per tenant and per caller, alerts that catch failures wherever they start, and logs you can search across regions.

 - Make deploys routine with canary and staged rollouts, so dependency and security upgrades stop being risky.

 - Redesign how the service works with Postgres at scale: reusing connections, limiting or streaming large results, and isolating and rate-limiting tenants, so no single caller, human or agent, can degrade it for everyone else.

 - Help decide the service’s long-term architecture with our Platform teams, then evolve it without breaking the callers that depend on it.

 - Write down and agree the service’s contract with its callers, including the dashboard, MCP and AI, and platform workers: how transactions, multi-statement queries, timeouts, and errors behave.

 - Work through incidents with the networking, Kubernetes, pooler, and control-plane teams when a problem on the path to customers’ databases starts in their systems.

 - Build backend services for code-first workflows, starting with delivering each branch’s configuration and secrets to the services that need them.

 - Make small changes directly in the CLI, dashboard, or docs when a capability needs them, with the owning team reviewing.

 - Review code and designs, mentor other engineers, and grow into leading the team’s technical direction.
   


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

Must have:

 - Have 5+ years of experience as a software engineer, most of it building and running backend services in production.

 - Have run a high-traffic, multi-tenant service in production: been on call for it, worked incidents through to resolution, and followed through on postmortems.

 - Write strong TypeScript, and work confidently in a large Node.js backend codebase.

 - Understand Postgres from the client side: connection management and pooling, transactions, statement timeouts and cancellation, and large result sets.

 - Have built observability for a service you owned (metrics, tracing, logs, and alerts tied to SLOs), and used it to debug problems that span proxies, load balancers, or Kubernetes.

 - Have kept a service healthy under load with patterns such as rate limiting, timeouts, memory limits, and graceful degradation.

 - Have shipped changes to a live service safely, with canaries, staged rollouts, feature flags, or fast rollback.

 - Work calmly and constructively with other teams during incidents, including when the root cause is in a system you don’t own.

 - Communicate clearly in writing, from design docs to postmortems, thrive in async, globally distributed teams, and make progress when the path isn’t fully defined.

Nice to have, roughly in order of how much they’d help:

 - Have rebuilt or migrated a live, high-traffic service without breaking its callers, using techniques such as shadow traffic, contract tests, or incremental replacement.

 - Have led the design of reliability work, such as tenant isolation, load shedding, or a staged-deploy pipeline, or set technical direction that other engineers built on.

 - Have built or operated a database proxy or connection pooler (such as PgBouncer, Supavisor, or pgcat), or an API gateway such as Envoy.

 - Have secured a service that runs SQL on its callers’ behalf: handling credentials safely, and limiting how much damage any one caller can do.

 - Multi-region AWS experience.

 - Experience with Fastify.

 - Production experience in a second backend language, such as Elixir or Go.

 - Experience with a secrets manager or key management service, such as HashiCorp Vault or AWS KMS.

 - Familiarity with Supabase, or with how AI agents use databases through tools like MCP.

ABOUT US


Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.


For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.


AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.


At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.


We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models.
